HarnessEvent.description:
A single normalized event emitted while a harness runs.

The common fields (timestamp and optional session ID) are carried alongside
the type specific [`EventKind`], which is flattened into the serialized form
so the type discriminator and its fields sit inline rather than under a
nested payload.

oneOf.description: A plain natural language message emitted by the agent.

The model's internal reasoning ("thinking") content, reported by harnesses
that expose it as a distinct stream from the agent's visible output. It is
kept separate from [`Agent`](EventKind::Agent) because reasoning is often
long and is a different kind of activity; callers can present it apart from
the visible message (the UI collapses it by default).

message.description: The text of the model's reasoning.

oneOf.description: A shell command the agent ran.

command.description: The shell command the agent attempted to run.

exitCode.description: The process exit code, when known.

isSuccess.description: Whether the command succeeded, when known.

workingDirectory.description: The directory the command ran from, when reported.

oneOf.description: A file read.

endLine.description: The inclusive end line read, when known.

isSuccess.description: Whether the read succeeded, when known.

startLine.description: The inclusive start line read, when known.

oneOf.description: A file write.

endLine.description: The inclusive end line written, when known.

isSuccess.description: Whether the write succeeded, when known.

startLine.description: The inclusive start line written, when known.

oneOf.description: A filesystem or in-file search.

isSuccess.description: Whether the search completed, when known.

path.description: The scope that was searched, when known.

query.description: The search pattern, glob, or file name searched for.

oneOf.description: A directory listing.

isSuccess.description: Whether the listing completed, when known.

path.description: The directory whose contents were listed, when known.

oneOf.description: Use of a skill, when the harness distinguishes it from a file read.

endLine.description: The inclusive end line read, when known.

isSuccess.description: Whether the skill use completed, when known.

path.description: The skill file that was read.

skillName.description: The harness provided skill name, when known.

startLine.description: The inclusive start line read, when known.

oneOf.description: Subagent orchestration activity.

action.description: The orchestration state the harness reported.

isSuccess.description: Whether the action completed successfully, when known.

subagentId.description: The harness provided subagent identifier, when known.

subagentName.description: The harness provided subagent name, when known.

oneOf.description: An error reported by the harness itself (not an agent caused error).

code.description: A harness provided stable error code, when one exists.

message.description: A human readable description of the error.

oneOf.description: A potential issue reported by the harness.

code.description: A harness provided stable warning code, when one exists.

message.description: A human readable description of the potential issue.

oneOf.description:
A run lifecycle stage reported by the orchestrator itself, rather than
translated from harness output. These mark the setup and teardown steps
that bracket a harness session — pulling the image, starting the
container, installing the harness, preparing the test case, and tearing
down — so a caller sees what is happening during steps that can take a
while instead of a silent wait before the harness's first event.

message.description: A human readable description of the stage and its status.

stage.description: The setup or teardown stage this event reports on.

status.description: Whether the stage is beginning, finished, or failed.

oneOf.description: Harness output that could not be classified as any other type.

sessionId.description: The underlying harness's session identifier, when one is known.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 time the event was observed by the testing harness.

LinksIn.description:
The resolved public links for a pushed run — the authoritative copies the
backend writes onto the stored record.

playableBuild.description:
The deployment URL the build tool reported, recorded verbatim. A pushed
run's build is playable (so it can be reviewed) even before publish.

sourceRepo.description: The public repository holding the run's generated source.

OrchestrationAction.description: The subagent orchestration states a harness can report.

oneOf.description: A subagent began running.
A subagent finished successfully.
A subagent failed.

SystemStage.description:
The setup and teardown stages of a run that the orchestrator reports as
[`EventKind::System`] events, in the order they occur around a harness
session.

oneOf.description: Pulling the run-container image.
Starting the run container.
Installing the harness's CLI into the running container.
Confirming the installed harness CLI is usable.
Running the test case's init command to prepare the workspace.
Collecting artifacts and stopping the container after the session.
The stage has begun.
The stage finished successfully.
The stage failed; the run will not proceed past it.

description:
The body of `POST /runs`, the **push** step: a finished run's
machine-generated record, its resolved public links, and its optional
recorded event stream. A push stores the run *without* a review and does not
make it public — the build is released so it can be reviewed, but the run is
excluded from the public snapshot until it is published (see
`POST /runs/{id}/publish`). Reviews are submitted separately to
`POST /runs/{id}/reviews`. Requires a bearer token; idempotent on `record.id`.

events.description:
The run's recorded normalized event stream (empty when the run recorded
none); stored verbatim and re-emitted to the snapshot once published.

record.description:
A full run record. Its `links` MAY be empty here; the `links` below are
authoritative and the backend writes them onto the stored record.
